svg.aria-label: Neutrally stable Lotka-Volterra orbits, the quarter-cycle lag between predator and prey, and the paradox of enrichment
svg.text: Neutrally stable orbits — the amplitude is set by where you started
Every orbit is closed. Perturb it and it stays on the new orbit.
A centre is the marginal case between a stable and an unstable
spiral — so ANY change to the model destroys it.
Helping the prey produces more PREDATORS.
The predator peak LAGS the prey peak
The predator’s numerical response needs a
generation, so it peaks a quarter cycle late.
Add a Type II response → destabilizes again.
A Type II response makes the prey isocline
HUMP-shaped. Raising K moves the hump right.
crossing RIGHT of the hump → stable spiral
crossing LEFT of the hump → growing limit cycle
Enrichment moved the hump under it.
More food → bigger swings → extinction at
the troughs. Monitor VARIANCE, not the mean.
